steps.text: Blend together butter and flour in a medium bowl. Mix in Cheddar cheese, salt, red pepper flakes, hot pepper sauce, and pecans. Form dough into a roll and wrap in parchment paper. Refrigerate dough 8 hours to overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Slice dough into very thin wafers and place onto a baking tray.
Bake wafers in the preheated oven until crisp, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheese Wafers
raw_recipe.description: The secret ingredients in this cheese wafers recipe are pungent spices like red pepper flakes and hot pepper sauce, along with crunchy chopped pecans.

review.reviewBody: I wanted a recipe for a cracker I could make in an old set of ice-box-cookie-molds. This is perfect! I made a batch according to the recipe and another one with a milder cheese and different seasoning. Both were great. One batch needed a little water to form a dough. (Perhaps it depends on the moisture content of the cheese.) Both batches sliced cleanly with no crumbling and held their shapes fine. Nice non-sweet treat!

A few changes are needed. Make sure both the cheese and butter are at room temperature and cream them together BEFORE adding the flour. This will help the dough come together. Also recommend adding a teaspoon of Worcestershire sauce. 
Other optional ingredients include smoked or regular paprika, which add both taste and color if you are using a white cheddar. 
If you want them crispy, you must slice them VERY thinly. I happen to like them a bit soft. You can also omit the chopped pecans, and put a pecan half on top of each wafer, secured with a bit of egg white for different look.

Read the other reviews and used 2 tsp steak seasoning in place of the salt, and used 12 oz extra sharp cheddar cheese, and melted the butter. Baked for 25 minutes until bottom of crackers were very brown. They came out delicious!

QUote good. I made two batches - one with Walnuts, the other with Chilli (so at least some were child friendly). Rather than adding all the cheese, I kept 1/2 back then put 1/3rd on rolled out pastry, folded in 3, turned & rolled again, then repeated twice more. This gave a nice - almost puff pastry - wafer, rather similar to a Dutch brand of Cheese Crispies - also used 50% cheddar, 50% gouda cheese.

The taste is really good but the method needs amending. The butter should be thoroughly creamed first. Stir in cheese, hot sauce and pepper flakes, THEN add the flour , etc., to make any kind of workable dough. I would also suggest finely chopping the nuts and that the wafers not be sliced any thinner than 1/4", otherwise they shatter during removal from baking pan.

I have been making these for a few years and they are really good ! I do not use pecans or any seasonings and they taste great that way. It is more time consuming, but I use a small shot glass as a cookie cutter to form the crackers. It makes twice as much and they are crispy !

Very good. Left out the red pepper flakes, and increased the pepper sauce just a bit - less spicy than my usual "Cheese Pennies" from Maida Heatters Book of Great Cookies pp. 269-270. Added a few TBSP. of heavy cream to dough at the end to make it a bit more malleable and hold together and make into a nice roll.
Add water to mixture to make a dough. Slice no less than 1/8 - 1/4 inches. Bake on non-stick sheet sprayed with baking spray or they may stick.
Has anyone rolled the dough between pieces of parchment and cut out the discs or shapes? Just wondering if it would be easier since some reviewers are saying its difficult to slice off the roll.
Seriously delicious and the reason I gained 2 pounds today :) Made this in food processor... added 1/4 c water ( 1T at a time) until dough came together. Baked 20 minutes.. yum. Major YUM!
I have made these Cheese Wafers for about 4 years and all my friends and neighbors love them. The only addition I make is that I add a little dry mustard. Very addictive.
Added smoked paprika. Sprinkled on top after baked.
They were easy to make and came out perfectly but tasted so bland. I will make them again, but I will spice them up a lot ;)
Very dry. Doesn't form a dough, so there's no way to roll it. I added water, then more water, then more water, and ultimately tossed it in the trash.
Fantastic recipe. Followed exactly and they turned out perfect.

So much better than another recipe that was an epic fail’! 
I did add a bit more cheese though . 

People really liked them !
Excellent ...made just as written. Use really really soft butter and it will come together better! I used my hands to mix!
They were more like a fluffy cookie/cracker. Not crunchy at all. Not sure what I did wrong.
These were good but very greasy....I used Longhorn colby and sunflower seeds. I may try them again using Cheddar but I think I'll stick to more healthy snacks. My crowd didn't eat them.
These were pretty good. I put all of the ingredients in my food processor - it worked great to make a dough - very easy. I think this would have been very difficult by hand.
